label: 1-2 steps after an input s, early in the original phase
explanation: Fires during the original-token phase on the one or two steps right after the letter s was input (prev_tok==s: 18x lift, about 74% of activation mass; prev2_tok==s covers most of the rest). It is limited to early positions: it peaks at t=3-4, is weak at t=6-7, and never fires at t=0 or t>=8. It is essentially silent on the delimiter step (1% of mass) and never fires in the copy phase. It is also not active on the s step itself, and it decays by three steps after s. On magnitude, the top examples (about 1.0 of max) all come right after a doubled s s (prev_tok and prev2_tok both s). A single preceding s gives about 0.45 of max, and s two steps back usually gives about 0.1-0.4. Firing is weaker or absent after a second, later occurrence of s and at positions t>=6. Missed activations are mostly tiny (bottom quartile) with no s nearby.

issues: Minor: the claim that it 'peaks at t=3-4' holds for firing rate (8.1-8.2%). By activation mass, t=3 is highest (0.35) and t=2 (0.25) is about equal to t=4 (0.25). This is a matter of wording, not an error.

Minor: prev2_tok==s without prev_tok==s is a weaker part of the predicate. Its test precision is 0.78 against 0.976 for prev_tok==s alone, so most of the false positives are steps where s was two back and the feature stayed quiet. That fits the explanation's 'usually 0.1-0.4' and 'decays' wording. Restricting the prev2 branch to t<=4 did not help (F1 0.804).

All other claims check out on the dev split. Nothing fires in the copy phase (0 steps). The delimiter step holds 1.2% of mass. Nothing fires at t=0 or t>=8. On the s step itself without a preceding s, precision is 0.022. Three steps after s, with no s at 1 or 2 back, precision is 0.095, so firing has decayed. Steps right after a doubled s s have precision 0.893, and the top examples are all s s followed by the next token at about 1.0. With t>=6 and an s nearby, precision is 0.084.

Test-split misses (32k steps, 4.7% of mass) are concentrated in the lowest activation quartile (28% coverage there, against 89-99.7% in the upper quartiles). They show no systematic token, position or history pattern. With t in 1..5 and no s seen yet, precision is 0.011, which is diffuse low-level noise. Adding s three back lowers F1 to 0.756.
